evidence: Quint. 1.5.47: prōnōmen quoque genus, numerum, cāsūs habet
terms.comment: The word that stands “for a noun”, prō nōmine: Traupman’s pupil defines it as pars ōrātiōnis quae prō nōmine pōnitur (Traupman 223). The kinds have the grammarians’ names, mostly late: a personal pronoun is prōnōmen persōnāle, a relative relātīvum, an interrogative interrogātīvum, a reflexive reciprocum (Priscian), a possessive possessīvum (Quint. 1.5.45), and a demonstrative dēmōnstrātīvum (Traupman 224); see those words. Traupman’s prōnōmen intentiōnis for an intensive pronoun (ipse) is not found in Lewis & Short. Varro calls the indefinite pronoun articulus īnfīnītus (Lewis & Short s.v. īnfīnītus).

terms.gloss: a pronoun, “a word used for another word”
terms.comment: An early grammarian’s word, cited by Varro; prōnōmen prevailed.

phrases.latin: prōnōmen quoque genus, numerum, cāsūs habet
phrases.english: the pronoun too has gender, number and case
